Since $3,$ $5,$ and $11$ are coprime, then according to the Chinese remainder theorem, the system has a unique solution modulo $3\cdot 5\cdot 11=165.$

We will solve the system in two steps.

**Step 1.** Find the common solution for the first and second congruences of the system.

From the first congruence, we get

$$
x≡0\,(\text{mod}\,3)\,⟹\,x=3t,\,t\in Z.
$$

Substituting this into the second congruence, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡4 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,5) \\ 3t & ≡4 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,5)\end{aligned}
$$

Since $5$ is a relatively small modulus, we can solve it by trial and error. We have that $2\cdot 3≡1\,(\text{mod}\,5).$ So, we multiply both sides by $2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3t & ≡4 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,5) \\ 2\cdot 3t & ≡8 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,5) \\ t & ≡3 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,5)\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $t=3+5s,$ where $s\in Z.$ Substituting this into the expression for $x,$ we get the common solution for the first and second congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =3t \\  & =3(3+5s) \\  & =9+15s\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2.** Find the common solution of all three congruences.

Now, substituting the common solution of the first two congruences into the third congruence, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡10 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,11) \\ 9+15s & ≡10 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,11) \\ 15s & ≡1 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,11) \\ 4s & ≡1 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,11)\end{aligned}
$$

Since $11$ is a relatively small modulus, by trial and error, we have that $3\cdot 4≡1\,(\text{mod}\,11).$ So, we multiply both sides by $3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4s & ≡1 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,11) \\ 3\cdot 4s & ≡3 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,11) \\ s & ≡3 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,11)\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $s=3+11u,$ where $u\in Z.$ Substituting this into the expression for the common solution of the first two congruences, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =9+15s \\  & =9+15(3+11u) \\  & =54+165u.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x≡54\,(\text{mod}\,165)$ is the unique solution modulo $165,$ and $x=54$ is the smallest natural number solution to the system.

x≡0(mod3)⟹x=3t,t∈Z.

x≡4(mod5)3t≡4(mod5)

Since 5 is a relatively small modulus, we can solve it by trial and error. We have that 2⋅3≡1(mod5). So, we multiply both sides by 2:

3t≡4(mod5)2⋅3t≡8(mod5)t≡3(mod5)

As a result, t=3+5s, where s∈Z. Substituting this into the expression for x, we get the common solution for the first and second congruences:

x=3t=3(3+5s)=9+15s

Step 2. Find the common solution of all three congruences.

Now, substituting the common solution of the first two congruences into the third congruence, we obtain the following:

x≡10(mod11)9+15s≡10(mod11)15s≡1(mod11)4s≡1(mod11)

Since 11 is a relatively small modulus, by trial and error, we have that 3⋅4≡1(mod11). So, we multiply both sides by 3:

4s≡1(mod11)3⋅4s≡3(mod11)s≡3(mod11)

As a result, s=3+11u, where u∈Z. Substituting this into the expression for the common solution of the first two congruences, we get

x=9+15s=9+15(3+11u)=54+165u.

Therefore, x≡54(mod165) is the unique solution modulo 165, and x=54 is the smallest natural number solution to the system.
